newsitem.title: UK: Strategy concerns send C&W shares seesawing.
newsitem.headline: Strategy concerns send C&W shares seesawing.

text.p: Concerns about Cable and Wireless's European strategy but relief that it had disentangled itself from its German venture with Veba on favourable terms caused the group's shares to seesaw on Friday.
The shares swung from a low of 472.5p to a high of 487p in brisk trade and some analysts said they remained unsure about what Cable and Wireless's European strategy now was.

"Some people are relieved C&W have come out of this alliance because it was seen in some quarters as not being good enough on the global front as a partnership with one of the other big three alliances," said Richard Jones, analyst at Yamaichi.
"On the other hand, people are saying this leaves a vacuum in terms of what they are now doing in Europe," he added.
C&W earlier confirmed a widely-expected move to abandon its alliance with Germany's Veba and RWE because the two sides disagreed about how to attack the German telecoms market.

Veba favoured a strategy of high cost infrastructre investments. C&W said it wanted to focus efforts in continental Europe on developing businesses to strengthen the position of its British-based Cable & Wireless Communications unit.

Martin Mabbutt, telecoms analyst at HSBC James Capel, said that if C&W had decided that Germany was simply too expensive to exploit via infrastructure investment it was "nice to see them being reaslistic".

But he added: "If it's a precursor to doing something more extensive, and I guess that has to be the assumption, then let's wait to see what it is before deciding whether what they've done is sensible or not."
Although C&W said earlier that it expected no imminent link up with a global alliance, analysts still believe the company will eventually link up with a partnership such as Global One.

C&W has been tipped as the "perfect partner" for Global One, a marriage between Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and America's Sprint, because it has access to two key markets Global One lacks -- Britain and Asia.
But analysts said they were concerned that although C&W no longer had to pay high start-up costs in Germany, this was merely a short-term benefit.
"It improves earnings in the short term and supposedly diminishes them longer-term," Mabbutt noted.
In the meantime, analysts remain unconvinced that C&W's European operations can be built up to become a force to be reckoned with as European telecoms markets are eased open in 1998.

C&W's remaining European operations are relatively small. Cable and Wireless Europe, which has operations in eight European countries, accrued losses of 16 million stg in the six months to September 30, 1996.
